question.text: Post Finance (No.2) Act 2024 (w.e.f. 23 July 2024), what is the holding period for a security to be treated as LONG-TERM capital asset in the following cases?

answer.text: Listed equity: > 36 months; Unlisted equity: > 36 months; Listed debentures: > 36 months

Listed equity / equity-oriented MF units / listed debentures / listed securities: > 12 months; unlisted securities other than unlisted bonds/debentures covered by the deemed-STC rule, including unlisted equity and LLP interest: > 24 months

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (pages 457-460), Finance (No.2) Act 2024, w.e.f. 23 July 2024, harmonised the long-term holding period: listed securities (including units of UTI, units of equity-oriented MFs, zero-coupon bonds and listed debentures) qualify as long-term if held for more than 12 months; unlisted securities (such as unlisted equity and LLP interest) qualify as long-term if held for more than 24 months. The Trap: Option A is the pre-23 July 2024 regime for unlisted debentures. Option B over-simplifies into a single bucket. Option C reflects an outdated boundary that no longer applies. Note: The workbook also carves out an exception: unlisted bonds or unlisted debentures transferred, redeemed or matured on or after 23 July 2024 are deemed short-term irrespective of holding period. Option D's wording reflects this exception so it cannot be read to include those instruments.
